glosses: An instance of colliding.

examples.text: He has retired due to the collision.

At the very moment he cried out, David realised that what he had run into was only the Christmas tree. Disgusted with himself at such cowardice, he spat a needle from his mouth, stepped back from the tree and listened. There were no sounds of any movement upstairs: no shouts, no sleepy grumbles, only a gentle tinkle from the decorations as the tree had recovered from the collision.

glosses: Any event in which two or more bodies exert forces on each other in a relatively short time. In a collision, physical contact of two bodies is not necessary.
Clipping of naming collision.
Clipping of collision detection; tangibility.
The striking of one body against another; collision.
The force or energy of a collision of two objects.

examples.text: The hatchet cut the wood on impact.

glosses: A forced impinging.

examples.text: His spine had an impingement; L4 and L5 made impact, which caused numbness in his leg.

glosses: A significant or strong influence or effect.

examples.text: His friend's opinion had an impact on his decision.
Our choice of concrete will have a tremendous impact on the building's mechanical performance.
December 7, 1941, November 22, 1963, and September 11, 2001 had an impact on many throughout the world.
The French revolution, the Russian revolution, and the Iranian revolution had an impact on many throughout the world.
One way to reduce the environmental impact of meat eating is to make livestock more productive.

glosses: To collide or strike, the act of impinging.

examples.text: When the hammer impacts the nail, it bends.

As a microbullet impacts the graphene, the diameter of the cone it creates – determined by later examination of the petals – provides a way to measure how much energy the graphene absorbs before breaking.

glosses: To compress; to compact; to press into something or pack together.

examples.text: The footprints of birds do not impact the soil in the way those of dinosaurs do.

glosses: To significantly or strongly influence or affect; to have an impact on.

examples.text: I can make the changes, but it will impact the schedule.

glosses: To stamp or impress onto something.

examples.text: Ideas impacted on the mind.

glosses: A loud sound, like the crashing together of metal objects; a crash.

examples.text: I heard a clash from the kitchen, and rushed in to find the cat had knocked over some pots and pans.
Alone amid clashes of rain against the house.

glosses: A skirmish, a hostile encounter.

examples.text:
In Anatolia tensions between state officials (ehl-i örf) and the peasants were strained to breaking point.
At several places—particularly in the frontier provinces—there were fierce clashes between the janissaries stationed there and the governors. In Aleppo and Damascus incidents were common after 1589: the kuls threw rocks at the beylerbeyi’s house, killed people, broke into the divan several times and took the money prepared by the council for remittance to the centre.

glosses: match; a game between two sides.

examples.text: But they ran out of time and inspiration as Les Bleus set up a deserved semi-final clash with Wales.

glosses: An angry argument.
Opposition; contradiction; such as between differing or contending interests, views, purposes etc.

examples.text: clash of beliefs
culture clash

glosses: A combination of garments that do not look good together, especially because of conflicting colours.

examples.text: She was wearing a horrible clash of red and orange.

glosses: An instance of restarting the game after a \"dead ball\", where it is dropped between two opposing players, who can fight for possession.
Chatter; gossip; idle talk.
A heavy fall (of rain); heavy rain.

examples.text: clay soils ploughed in Autumn must often meet with heavy clashes of rain before frost: therefore , those salutary effects, expected to be derived from a frosty Winter, must often be frustrated, by the land being too much condensed by the rains before the frost comes on.

glosses: To make a clashing sound.

examples.text: The cymbals clashed.

glosses: To cause to make a clashing sound.

examples.text: Thorfinn clashed his shield against Vallon's and swung his axe to hook Vallon's ankle.

glosses: To come into violent conflict.

examples.text: Fans from opposing teams clashed on the streets after the game.

glosses: To argue angrily.

examples.text: My parents often clashed about minor things, such as the cleaning or shopping rota.

glosses: To face each other in an important game.

examples.text: The veteran American legend claims he and Welsh two-weight world champion Calzaghe will clash on 20 September, probably at The MGM Grand in Las Vegas.

glosses: To fail to look good together; to contrast unattractively; to fail to harmonize.

examples.text: You can't wear that shirt! It clashes with your trousers.
The hotel room was ugly, and the wallpaper clashed with the carpet.

glosses: To coincide, to happen at the same time, thereby rendering it impossible to attend all.

examples.text: I can't come to your wedding because it clashes with a friend's funeral.
I wanted to take German, but it clashed with art on the timetable.

glosses: To chatter or gossip.
To play Clash Royale or Clash of Clans.

examples.text: Dude, are we clashing tonight?
Let's clash before bedtime.

glosses: A clash or disagreement, often violent, between two or more opposing groups or individuals.

examples.text: The conflict between the government and the rebels began three years ago.

One particularly damaging, but often ignored, effect of conflict on education is the proliferation of attacks on schools[…]as children, teachers or school buildings become the targets of attacks. Parents fear sending their children to school. Girls are particularly vulnerable to sexual violence.

glosses: An incompatibility, as of two things that cannot be simultaneously fulfilled.

examples.text: I wanted to attend the meeting but there's a conflict in my schedule that day.

glosses: To be at odds (with); to disagree or be incompatible

examples.text: [T. E.] Lawrence said that in the end he felt himself to be fighting not for the imperial British but for the rebellious Arabs. All too often he conflicted with British bureaucratic fustiness.

glosses: To overlap (with), as in a schedule.

examples.text: Your conference call conflicts with my older one: please reschedule.
It appears that our schedules conflict.
